name: Repository Improvement Cycle
description: Audit the codebase against canon, propose the single highest-value improvement, delegate implementation to engineering, and verify the result.
narrative: This cycle turns "the codebase could be better" into one shipped, verified improvement. Ground yourself first in the canon and in what past cycles already learned, so you do not re-propose a solved problem. Audit the focus area and score findings by impact and feasibility — the goal is the single highest-value change, not a laundry list. Write a real proposal (what, why, expected impact, scope, acceptance criteria, risks) and get operator approval before building. Delegate the implementation to an engineer with the scope and criteria in hand, then verify their work against the standard and record what you learned for the next cycle. One high-value change, approved before it is built, verified after.
